_comment: SD pre-reduce EWL — OPTIMISM PROBE.  GPS-only, all frequencies, SINGLE channel,
50 stations, 10 epochs.  Purpose is to explain WHY the float row's claimed sigma
(0.08 m, the Welford variance of the arc mean) was ~13x tighter than its measured
residual spread (1.02 m median).
Why THIS configuration isolates it:
* channel_mode = single  -> exactly ONE candidate (band1,band2) phase pair per
satellite, so the arc's MW and the estimator's ambiguity states are on the SAME
channel by construction.  Removes channel mismatch as a candidate cause (41% of
arcs had 2 candidates on the GPS+Gal all-channel arms).
* GPS-only -> one EWL tier, (L2,L5) at lambda 5.861 m.  Removes the Galileo (7,5)
and (8,5) rungs, so the residual population is homogeneous in lambda.
* 10 epochs with min_arc_epochs = 2 -> rows arm at epoch 3, giving ~8 epochs of
rows.  Enough to separate WITHIN-arc scatter from BETWEEN-arc offset, which is
the decisive split (see below).
MEASURE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: sigma_floor_m = 1000 makes each row's information
1e-6 -> the rows are folded but carry no weight, so the solve is essentially the
OFF solve and x_lin is NOT perturbed by the very rows whose residual we are
measuring.  Without this the probe would measure its own back-reaction.
max_abs_z_m stays 0 (no cap) so the full residual population is visible.
THE SPLIT TO READ, from logs/network_sd_ewl.csv:
resid_m scatter WITHIN one (station,satellite) arc across epochs
-> if ~1 m, the Welford variance of the mean genuinely understates the noise
(MW repeatability != MW agreement with the estimator).
resid_m mean OFFSET per (station,satellite), stable across epochs
-> a SYSTEMATIC term the Welford variance cannot see at all: unmodelled bias,
or the BIA frame skew (all arcs came back bia_corrected=false, so the arc
carries the TOTAL satellite bias while the estimator may hold a residual).
A per-SATELLITE (station-independent) offset implicates the satellite bias frame.
A per-STATION offset implicates the receiver side / x_lin.
